motion_rule: the cart carries him across frame every beat and he never steps off it; crates and ice sweep past the lens; the camera tracks alongside at his muzzle height; new shot size each beat, never wider than his muzzle filling a third of frame; ONE sideways move per beat, never up or down, never a chain; the row tears past in the punch beat too
character: a lean grey wolf with a scarred muzzle, riding a low flat market cart, one hind paw scooting it along, yellow eye always clear
second_characters: ONE hog docker, going right to left a step from the lens and crossing frame himself, working wide in every spoken beat, chewing his own whole fish from 4.30, never lifting the wolf off the cart
props: ONE bare fish spine, picked clean, see-through, nothing written on it; ONE whole fish in the hog trotters; crates of fish; a barrel
prop_continuity: the spine rides in his paw to 9.00, then flies over his shoulder; the whole fish stays with the hog
environment: a fish row under daylight, counters and crates packed tight both sides, no far wall, no bare stretch
light_events: hard white noon off the ice, a side shaft through the gaps of the spine at 3.20, another on his muzzle at 6.60

audio.language: Russian, lines verbatim; latin hints never spoken
audio.delivery: a dry angry male voice, biting off each word, 4.2 syllables/sec
audio.pacing: 0.00-2.85 and 2.85-4.30 each one breath, the first word starts at 0.00; after 4.30 not a word, sfx keep going
audio.lip_sync: his jaw opens on every syllable
audio.sfx: cart wheels, ice cracking, crates banging, chewing

timeline.a: the hog shoves the bare spine at him and one yank tears it out of the trotter
he shoves the spine out sideways on a straight paw, right across frame
he swings the spine like an oar and shoves off a crate with it
he whips the spine across frame and it rattles
he kicks off a counter as the hog hauls a crate past the lens the other way
he rakes the spine through the daylight shaft on a straight paw, light strobing through the gaps between its ribs
the hog tears a bite off his whole fish a step from the lens, the wolf batting a hanging chain aside with the spine
he drags the spine along the crates and it clatters, the hog rolling a barrel at the lens the other way
he swings the spine across to his cheek and turns straight into the lens, the ribs a paw from his eye
he drives his muzzle at the lens through the spine, the hog muzzle chewing that same fish right in the gap between the ribs over his shoulder
he licks his chops and shoves the cart on with one drive of the paw, crates whipping past
still rolling he cracks a rib off the spine in his teeth and spits it out
he hurls the spine over his shoulder and cuts his eye at the hog, riding on

must_appear: the hog gives him the spine at 0.00 and keeps the whole fish; the wolf never leaves the moving cart; the spine is in his paw every beat to 9.00; light through its gaps at 3.20-4.30; at 6.60-7.20 the chewing hog muzzle sits in the gap between the ribs, the wolf eye and nose clear of it; every word spoken, the last by 4.30
negative_prompt: subtitles, watermark, letterbox, night, dark scene, a static camera, a still background, standing in place, an inscription, a label, a stamp, digits, cyrillic letters, slow motion, a closed jaw while speaking, a hero moving up or down the frame, multiple wolves, clothing on the wolf, a hero lifted off the cart, a second fish spine, a whole fish in the wolf paw
